lines: Revenue Growth: $35M (2024) → $63.9M (2026 est.) = +83% in two years (E-053). This growth reflects both organic AUM appreciation and the Roosevelt Investments integration (May 2024).
AUM Growth: $23.6B at CI acquisition (Apr 2021) → $25.4B (Mar 2024) = +7.6% over 3 years. 13F equity: $7.1B (Q2 2025).

M&A History: Four acquisitions integrated: Philadelphia International Advisors (2015), Denver Investment Advisors (2018), Roosevelt Investments (2024), plus Barrett Asset Management was acquired by CI Financial in the same wave but operates separately.
Parent Context: Corient platform: $224B aggregate. Mubadala backing brings sovereign-fund discipline. SBH is one of 14+ RIAs in the CI/Corient family, each at different stages of FSC standardization.

firmographics.narrative_md:
CI Segall Bryant & Hamill (SBH) is a Chicago-headquartered, SEC-registered investment adviser founded in 1994, managing approximately $25.4 billion in combined AUM/AUA as of March 2024 (INT-005:F1). The firm is wholly owned within a multi-layered corporate structure: SBH reports to Corient Management LLC, which sits under Corient Holdings Inc., itself a subsidiary of CI Financial Corp. (TSX:CIX, NYSE:CIXX). In August 2025, CI Financial was taken private by Mubadala Capital (Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund) at C$12.1B enterprise value (E-078). SBH operates from six U.S. offices — Chicago (HQ), Denver, Philadelphia (Ardmore), St. Louis, Naples FL, and Cincinnati OH — with 115–124 employees (INT-005:F2). The firm serves institutional clients (foundations, endowments, pension plans), intermediary channels, and high-net-worth individuals through 27+ investment strategies, 16 mutual funds, 1 ETF (USSE), 9 collective investment trusts, and 3+ private funds (INT-005).

SBH’s stated mission is "to exceed our clients’ expectations by helping them realize their long-term investment goals across complex market environments and by delivering a customized, high-touch service experience. The result is long-lasting relationships with our clients built on trust" (E-084, SBH About Us page). This mission anchors all strategic priorities and defines how technology investments — including the current FSC migration — should be evaluated.
